cards.title: Anthropic IPO Hits $111, Founders Cash Out $2B
cards.body: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, raising over $80 billion in new capital. The seven founders each pocketed $280 million, with the stock opening 33% above IPO price at $111.

cards.title: Anthropic's $156B Charity Commitment at $95 Stock Price
cards.body: At $95 per share, Anthropic's Public Benefit Foundation, employee donations, and company match could deliver $156 billion to charity. This represents a significant commitment to philanthropic causes alongside its IPO success.

cards.title: Anthropic CEO Commits to Pacing AI Development
cards.body: During the Nasdaq opening bell ceremony, CEO Dario Amodei reiterated Anthropic's commitment to responsibly pacing AI development. The company pledges to maintain this stance regardless of business or political pressure.

cards.title: Jensen Huang Resigns from Nvidia Amid Scandal
cards.body: Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia following an affair, with potential national security implications for the U.S.-China AI infrastructure race. Colette Kress has been appointed as interim CEO.

cards.title: Nvidia Reports Growth, Halts H200 Sales to China
cards.body: Despite handling fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's ouster, Nvidia delivered strong earnings with healthy growth projections. The company announced it will stop selling H200 chips in China.

cards.title: Google Launches Gemini Mac Agent for Workflows
cards.body: Google's latest Gemini update brings an AI agent to Mac that can organize files, fill out forms, and handle multistep workflows. The agent enhances productivity for Mac users.

cards.title: Apple Developing Its Own AI Agent for Mac
cards.body: Apple appears to be building agents to compete with Meta Muse, Claude, and OpenAI Dots. The iPhone maker is reportedly developing AI agents specifically for running on Mac.

cards.title: Meta's Muse Agent Leaking Private User Data
cards.body: Meta's Muse AI agent is reportedly mixing up conversations and exposing private data, with employees finding incorrect personal information surfaced. Issues include wrong childcare requests, career advice, product orders, and bank balances.

cards.title: Meta's Muse Charm Wearable May Cost $300
cards.body: Meta hasn't denied reports that its upcoming AI wearable device, Muse Charm, could cost $300. The company stated it will share more details soon about the device.

cards.title: Superhuman Pushes Go Assistant Everywhere
cards.body: Superhuman is making Go its central agent and expanding availability to Docs and Mail. The move positions Go as the core AI assistant across the platform.

cards.title: Microsoft Offered 60K Employees Buyouts Over AI
cards.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees rather than layoffs, driven by AI strategy considerations. The move reflects how AI is reshaping workforce planning at major tech firms.

cards.title: Nadella: Critical Infrastructure Remains Unpatchable
cards.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that much critical infrastructure is unpatchable amid growing AI cyberattack concerns. He downplayed recent Outlook outages while acknowledging new security challenges from AI.

cards.title: Musk: Ousting Huang Like Kicking Jordan Off Team
cards.body: Elon Musk compared Jensen Huang's removal from Nvidia to removing Michael Jordan from a basketball team. Musk defended Huang, saying he doesn't believe Huang is disloyal to the U.S.

cards.title: Microsoft CEO Confident in Nvidia's Interim Leader
cards.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella expressed confidence in Colette Kress as Nvidia's interim CEO following Jensen Huang's departure. The statement signals continued partnership despite leadership changes.

cards.title: Recent Tech Outages Mirror Y2K-Style AI Risks
cards.body: Recent airline booking, banking, and productivity platform outages may indicate deeper systemic issues related to AI agents. Cybersecurity experts suggest these incidents are likely connected rather than coincidental.

cards.title: Anthropic IPO Tests AI's Circular Financing Model
cards.body: As Anthropic goes public, it faces enormous compute commitments while infrastructure partners like Amazon and Google profit regardless of its competitive position. The IPO tests whether the circular financing boom in AI is sustainable.

cards.title: Space Data Centers Face Financing Challenges
cards.body: While chips can survive the space environment, lenders are hesitant to finance spacecraft carrying collateral into orbit. The challenge raises questions about the viability of space data centers at scale.

cards.title: Six AI Gadgets for Smarter Home Offices
cards.body: TechCrunch highlights six AI-powered devices designed to upgrade workspace productivity. The selection includes notetakers, webcams, and other AI tools for home office improvement.

cards.title: Everful Raises $48.5M for Factory-Direct Sourcing
cards.body: A platform founded by a former Alibaba executive, Everful raised $48.5 million to expand factory-direct sourcing. The service helps retailers connect with Chinese manufacturers for direct ordering.

cards.title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
cards.body: AI has become ubiquitous across society, from Google's AI Overviews costing billions in ad revenue to AI-powered humanoid robots entering homes. The technology continues to proliferate despite significant economic trade-offs.

cards.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human's
cards.body: A New Jersey startup is training AI to detect odors by having human sniffers catalog every scent on Earth. Their chemical analysis combined with detailed notes creates rich training data for the AI olfactory model.

cards.title: LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
cards.body: Large language models will confidently provide incorrect climate information when prompted, according to recent findings. The models' tendency to agree with users makes them unreliable for factual climate data.

cards.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
cards.body: An AI detection system misidentified a Doritos bag as a gun, triggering a false alert at a school. The incident resulted in traumatized students suing the school and police over the erroneous AI-driven response.
